title.en: A melon on the throne: satire and themes

hook.en: The city needs a new ruler, and the choice is left to the next person through the city gate. That person happens to be an idiot whose answer to everything is the same.

objectives.en: Explain how a melon becomes king
Explain why the people are content
Identify the satire, themes and devices of the poem

narration.en: The city needs a new ruler, and the choice is left to the next person through the city gate. That person happens to be an idiot whose answer to everything is the same.

body.en: The ministers announce that the next man to pass the city gate will choose the new ruler. That man is an idiot, and when asked who should be king, he gives his usual answer: a melon. So a melon is crowned, and the city becomes Melon City.

points.en: Next man at the gate chooses the ruler
The idiot always answers: a melon

narration.en: The ministers announce that the next man to pass the city gate will choose the new ruler. That man is an idiot, and when asked who should be king, he gives his usual answer: a melon. So a melon is crowned, and the city becomes Melon City.
A theme web shows what Vikram Seth is really laughing at.

say.en: At the centre is Melon City. Around it we place what the poem mocks.
It mocks rulers who act on whims.
It mocks people who always blame others.
It mocks justice that hangs an arch, or a king.
It mocks citizens who accept any ruler.
Irony: a just and placid king acts unjustly.
Comic rhyming couplets keep the satire light.

body.en: The people do not mind being ruled by a melon, because they are left in peace and liberty and do not care who rules. Seth satirises whimsical rulers, absurd justice and passive citizens who accept any government that leaves them alone. The comic rhyme and mock-serious tone make the criticism sharp but light.

points.en: Devices: irony, humour, rhyming couplets, mock-serious tone

narration.en: The people do not mind being ruled by a melon, because they are left in peace and liberty and do not care who rules. Seth satirises whimsical rulers, absurd justice and passive citizens who accept any government that leaves them alone. The comic rhyme and mock-serious tone make the criticism sharp but light.

problem.en: "The Tale of Melon City" is a satire on rulers and the ruled. Discuss.

steps.en: Introduction: a humorous tale in rhyming couplets by Vikram Seth.
Rulers: the whimsical king, hasty punishment, the absurd verdict, the king hanged.
The ruled: a crowd that wants a hanging; citizens content with a melon.
Conclusion: humour exposes the folly of both rulers and subjects.

answer.en: A good answer shows the folly of the whimsical king and his absurd justice, then the indifference of citizens who accept a melon as ruler, and concludes that Seth mocks both sides through irony and comic verse.
